Bug_Title: RV: Bad attempt to compute absolute value of signed 32-bit hashcode (RV_ABSOLUTE_VALUE_OF_HASHCODE)
Bug_Details:
This code generates a hashcode and then computes
the absolute value of that hashcode.  If the hashcode
is Integer.MIN_VALUE, then the result will be negative as well (since
Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) == Integer.MIN_VALUE).
 One out of 2^32 strings have a hashCode of Integer.MIN_VALUE,
including "polygenelubricants" "GydZG_" and ""DESIGNING WORKHOUSES".
 Integer.MIN_VALUE Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) == Integer.MIN_VALUE
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the line containing the `Math.abs(hashCode)` function call. If the `hashCode` variable happens to be `Integer.MIN_VALUE`, then the `Math.abs` function will return the same value, causing the resulting `absoluteValue` variable to be negative.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test result shows that the input string 'polygenelubricants' returns a hash code of Integer.MIN_VALUE, which is then passed to the Math.abs() function, resulting in a negative value. This confirms the triggering of the bug as described in the bug information.
